chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from some of our companions, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from a man of Quraysh from the people of Makkah, who said:

Sufyān al-Thawrī said, "Take us to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad." He said: So I went with him to him, and we found him having mounted his animal. Sufyān said to him, "O Abū ʿAbdillāh, narrate to us the hadith of the sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in Masjid al-Khayf." He said, "Leave me until I go for my need, for I have already mounted; when I return, I will narrate it to you." So he said, "I ask you by your kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that you narrate it to me now." He said: So he dismounted, and Sufyān said to him, "Order for me an inkpot and paper so that I may record it." So he called for it.

Then he said, "Write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. The sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in Masjid al-Khayf: May Allah brighten a servant who hears my statement, retains it, and conveys it to one whom it did not reach. O people, let the present convey to the absent. For perhaps a carrier of fiqh is not himself a faqīh, and perhaps a carrier of fiqh conveys it to one more understanding than he. Three things are such that the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously toward them: sincerity of action for Allah, giving sincere counsel to the Imams of the Muslims, and adherence to their جماعت, for their call encompasses those behind them. The believers are brothers; their blood is equal, and they are one hand against those besides them; the least of them may undertake their covenant."

So Sufyān wrote it, then presented it to him, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mounted. Sufyān and I departed, and when we were on part of the road, he said to me, "Stay where you are until I examine this hadith." So I said to him, "By Allah, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام has bound something upon your neck that will never leave your neck, ever." He said, "And what is that?"

I said to him, "Three things toward which the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously: sincerity of action for Allah—we know that. But as for giving sincere counsel to the Imams of the Muslims, who are these Imams whose sincere counsel is obligatory upon us? Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, and everyone whose testimony is not admissible with us and behind whom salat is not valid? And his saying, 'adherence to their جماعت'—then which جماعت? A Murjiʾī who says that whoever does not perform salat, does not fast, does not perform ghusl from janābah, demolishes the Kaʿbah, and marries his mother is still upon the faith of Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl? Or a Qadarī who says that what Allah عزّ وجلّ wills does not occur, while what Iblīs wills does occur? Or a Ḥarūrī who dissociates himself from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and bears witness against him with kufr? Or a Jahmī who says that it is only the knowledge of Allah alone, and iman is nothing other than that?"

He said, "Woe to you, then what do they say?" I said, "They say that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, by Allah, is the Imam whose sincere counsel is obligatory upon us, and that adherence to their جماعت means the people of his household." He said: So he took the document and tore it up, then said, "Do not inform anyone of it."

key_terms.إِخْلَاصُ الْعَمَلِ: sincerity and purity of intention in deeds done for Allah
key_terms.النَّصِيحَةُ: sincere counsel, loyalty, and faithful commitment
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely significant leader whose obedience and counsel are due
key_terms.خُطْبَةُ: the sermon or address being narrated from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.لِأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: to the rightful leaders of the Muslims
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الْخَيْفِ: the mosque at Minā where the prophetic sermon was delivered

ai.seo_question: Who are the Imams of the Muslims referred to in the sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله at Masjid al-Khayf?
ai.summary: This report narrates the sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in Masjid al-Khayf and then shows how its phrases concerning the Imams of the Muslims and adherence to their community were understood in relation to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام and Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It highlights the transmission of prophetic teaching, sincerity for Allah, and the question of legitimate religious authority within the Muslim community.
